entry.title: MMFlash: Faster Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models. Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model.
entry.summary:
Speculative decoding accelerates generation by letting a lightweight drafter propose tokens for parallel verification by a target model. Diffusion drafters such as DFlash propose an entire token block in a single forward pass, but mainly focus on text-only tasks, leaving multimodal drafting underexplored. To study this setting, we first introduce a metric of token-level visual dependence based on the KL divergence between next-token distributions with and without visual input.

entry.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
entry.summary:
Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #clean-tech #computer-vision

entry.title: VibePrevisBench: Evaluating Agentic Coding for 4D Scene Generation in Blender
entry.summary:
Controllable real-world video generation models can condition on a rendered graybox proxy video, which fixes layout, motion and camera. Coding agents can build such videos by reconstructing a 4D scene in Blender, yet no benchmark checks both these videos and the long, multi-shot scenes behind them. We introduce VibePrevisBench, a benchmark for 4D scene reconstruction: an agent turns a brief into an executable 4D scene and renders its proxy video.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: Gamer: A Generalist Vision-Language-Action Foundation Model for Long-Horizon Real-Time Game Agent
entry.summary:
We introduce Gamer, a generalist agent framework built for long-horizon tasks in complex interactive environments. Its end-to-end architecture combines perception, memory management, and multi-step reasoning. A shared training and deployment pipeline supports interaction with both conventional 2D graphical interfaces and complex 3D simulated worlds.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics #agents

entry.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
entry.summary:
Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #cryptography #databases

entry.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
entry.summary:
Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #clean-tech #computer-vision

entry.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems. The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics.
entry.summary:
The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents #robotics

entry.title: MIRIX-2.0: Multi-Agent Memory System. Long-term memory lets LLM agents personalize, stay consistent, and reuse what worked before.
entry.summary:
Long-term memory lets LLM agents personalize, stay consistent, and reuse what worked before. Parametric memories need training, consolidation can lose details for good, and keeping every record leaves a growing store to search. We present MIRIX-2.0, a multi-agent memory system designed to be practical, accurate, and efficient at once.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #combinatorics #agents

entry.title: V-JEPA-LM: Video-Language Models That Read Dynamics Beyond Static, Text-Aligned Representations
entry.summary:
World-model video encoders such as V-JEPA learn how scenes change (direction, speed, order, state) from video alone. To answer questions, they are joined to a language model trained on captions and question-answer pairs. But each caption or question names only a few attributes of a clip, so the model learns to retrieve those attributes rather than to read the clip, and the dynamics the encoder carries go unused: on the same items, a linear probe reads speed from frozen V-JEPA features at 87% while the VLM answers at chance.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process. Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph.
entry.summary:
Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph. We establish the exact conditions for attaining equality in the moving particle lemma for the interchange process on $G$ subject to a unit voltage drop across two terminal vertices $x\neq y \in V$. First, equality can occur only in irreducible representations indexed by partitions with at most two rows.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #probability-stats

entry.title: Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order
entry.summary:
Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #cryptography

entry.title: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games
entry.summary:
The questions of voting rights, group membership, and the boundaries of acceptable discourse all involve a recursive, self-stability issue, wherein the voters, group members, and acceptable commentators are often the ultimate arbiters of their own rules for inclusion and exclusion. In order to understand how ideological or issue diversity may impact the stability of such inclusion and exclusion, we introduce franchise elections, where voting members of a group vote to change the electorate. In particular, when agents are positioned inside an ideological or issue space, a social choice function that aggregates agent viewpoints induces a preference for agents over group composition, where agents prefer groups that improve the social choice function outcome for them.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #market-design

entry.title: A Push Down the Mountain: Framing Effects and Internal State Interventions on Collusive Behavior in a Long-Horizon LLM Agent
entry.summary:
Can sustained gain-loss (valence) framing sway an LLM agent toward market manipulation? We place Gemma 3 12B into the seat of a defendant in the London silver-fixing litigation, in a market simulation built from real case transcripts. Across 260 simulations, the agent is asked to collude on the price of silver by a counterparty.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #ml-theory #llm

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of the Influencer's Game in Resource Landscapes
entry.summary:
Across domains as varied as ecology, economics, and online platforms, individuals are incentivized to position themselves within resource-rich strategy spaces. In this work we introduce a new spatial game framework called the influencer's game. Within this new framework players' strategies are represented as positions within a trait space.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #market-design

entry.title: Unequal Rewards and the Direction of Scientific Work: Evidence from U.S. Public Universities
entry.summary:
Research on pay dispersion has long asked whether unequal rewards increase or depress performance. Tournament theory expects stronger effort, while social comparison accounts expect withdrawal. Both perspectives, however, treat performance as a single scale on which workers can be ranked.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #complex-systems

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Welfare: Evaluating AI Buyers under Strategic Price Complexity in a Synthetic Duopoly
entry.summary:
AI buying agents may alter sellers' incentives as well as consumers' decisions. In a synthetic duopoly, we evaluate price-comparison pipelines on a fixed menu and in empirical correlated-equilibrium games. Calculator assistance selects an optimal offer 84.00% of the time, versus 68.57% under verified-total disclosure, yet disclosure has a 20.14-unit higher consumer-worst equilibrium surplus.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #quant-finance

entry.title: Beyond Blossom: Accelerating MWPM Decoding for Surface Codes With Local Predecoding and Architecture-Aware Optimizations
entry.summary:
Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is widely used to decode surface codes, but its computational cost increases with code distance. We present Beyond Blossom, a state-of-the-art CPU-based MWPM decoder for surface codes. It combines algorithmic optimization through local predecoding, architecture-aware optimization, and pipeline-wide parallelism to reduce matching workload and execution overhead while preserving MWPM optimality.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter

entry.title: Topological phase diagram of an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with negative coupling
entry.summary:
Recently, an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with three atoms per unit cell has been experimentally realized in perovskite exciton-polariton micropillars. A distinctive feature of this system is that the second and third bands undergo a topological transition through a band crossing at the wave vector $k=0$, associated with a negative coupling. In this work, we analytically determine the phase diagram of the model as a function of the on-site energy splitting and the ratio of intercell to intracell hopping amplitudes.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #optics-photonics

entry.title: High Entropy Oxides as Room Temperature Anderson Insulators with Colossal Soft Gaps
entry.summary:
The Anderson effect, arising from destructive quantum interference of electron wave packets in disordered potentials, is usually observed at cryogenic temperatures and typically arises from extrinsic defects in conventional materials such as phosphorus dopants in silicon or oxygen vacancies in transition metal oxides. Here we demonstrate that a multication lattice of transition metals in a high-entropy oxide (HEO) natively establishes an interacting Anderson insulator that extends up to $500\,\mathrm{K}$. By controlling the population of transition metal cations in $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}_{1-x}(\mathrm{Cr},\mathrm{Fe},\mathrm{Co},\mathrm{Ni})_{x/4}\mathrm{O}_3$ (LS5B), we tune the system from the prototypical correlated metal $\mathrm{La}_{0.7}\mathrm{Sr}_{0.3}\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{O}_3$ at $x=0.00$ to a localized insulator at $x=0.80$, where the disorder length contracts to near the unit cell (3.85 $\mathring{\mathrm{A}}$) and drives the electron mean free path to the Ioffe-Regel limit.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #post-quantum

entry.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures
entry.summary:
Atomic disorder offers a potent degree of freedom to tailor material properties, yet the resulting vast configuration space obscures structure-property relations and hinders rational inverse design. Here we introduce Graph Amorphous Diffusion Transformer (GaDiT), a generative model that combines dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning and an interval-weighted training-noise distribution. GaDiT generates high-quality disordered structures while accelerating sampling by two orders of magnitude compared with existing corrector-based approaches, as demonstrated across two-dimensional amorphous carbon and three-dimensional amorphous silicon and silica.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #ml-theory

entry.title: Number fluctuations and particle loss in Dicke superradiance
entry.summary:
Dicke superradiance, the collective spontaneous emission of identical quantum emitters into a common reservoir, produces a burst with a characteristic delay $t_{\mathrm{SR}}$ and a peak intensity that scales quadratically with the emitter number $N$. This strong dependence makes the burst sensitive to how many emitters actually participate. In experiments, however, this number is rarely fixed: it fluctuates between preparations and decreases during emission through atom loss.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #optics-photonics

entry.title: Uniaxial strain induces $d$-wave phonon chirality in ferroelectric BaTiO$_3$
entry.summary:
Circularly dichroic resonant inelastic x-ray scattering has revealed electrically switchable $g$-wave phonon chirality in freestanding BaTiO$_3$ membranes. Here, we show from first principles that uniaxial strain changes the angular class of this texture. Lowering $C_{4v}$ to $C_{2v}$ adds a $d$-wave helicity that is bilinear in the orthorhombic strain $η$ and the polarization, with nodal lines along the stress axis.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science

entry.title: Bond Anharmonicity in a Caged Molecule Probed by Vibronic Core Spectroscopy
entry.summary:
X-ray absorption spectroscopy and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at the nitrogen K-edge show that the N$\equiv$N bond in N$_2$@C$_{60}$ is substantially more anharmonic than in free N$_2$, with the ground-state ($X^1Σ_g^+$) anharmonic constant $\hbarω_e x_e$ a factor of two larger ($3.8\pm0.3$~meV versus $\sim 1.8$~meV) despite an essentially unchanged harmonic frequency. The same enhancement is found across all three vibronic potentials accessible to the experiment---the electronic ground state, the core-excited intermediate state, and the spectator-decay final state---pointing to a common origin rather than an effect specific to one electronic configuration. High-level coupled-cluster calculations of the N$_2$@C$_{60}$ potential energy surface, however, find no significant change in anharmonicity upon encapsulation, ruling out a simple static distortion of the N$\equiv$N bonding potential by the fullerene cage.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science

entry.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments. We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories.
entry.summary:
We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #quantum-computing #infosec

entry.title: Nesting in additive manufacturing using quantum annealing
entry.summary:
Nesting in powder bed fusion (PBF), an additive manufacturing (AM) process, determines the positions and orientations of parts within the build space and influences build height and build time. As the number of parts and feasible placements increases, the nesting problem becomes computationally demanding. Exact approaches are limited to small problem sizes as computational effort increases rapidly with the problem size, while heuristic and metaheuristic approaches involve a trade-off between solution quality and computation time.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #quantum-computing #optimization
